text:
lucy: quick pulse — ran a host-only perf run on a baseline dedicated node using the 20-token chat payload. seeing an extra ~22ms before runtime decode. looks like preparse + framing + smallwrites.
tony: can you dump the stack sample or flame?
lucy: paste snippet: 
```
# top stacks (host samples)
preparse::tokenize_line -> 12.6ms
http2::framer::read_frame ->  4.1ms
grpc::decode_message     ->  2.2ms
socket::recv_into_iovec  ->  1.0ms
kvcache::lookup_shard    ->  2.3ms (miss spikes)
writev (syscall)         ->  1.8ms (many smallwrites)
```
sam: odd — kernel selection work shouldn't affect host parse. did we flip the preparse batch hint in PR #1476? iirc that set batch_hint=1 for tiny flows.
andrew: PR #1498 touched net coalesce and vhost write batching (net: coalesce-small-write flag). both merged last week. could be a combinatorial effect.
tony: kvcache miss spikes are worrying. what's shard distribution look like?
lucy: enabling KVCACHE_DEBUG shows 40% miss for these short requests on canary vs 18% on stable. keys are more distributed across 16 shards now vs 8.
sam: that matches the sharding change in #1476 actually. increased shard count reduces per-shard hit density for short-lived prefixes.
andrew: hypothesis: more shards -> more cold shards -> more misses -> extra blocking on kvcache hotpath -> backpressure in preparse -> smaller batches -> more smallwrites -> more http2 framing overhead.
lucy: repro steps I'm using: single-request driver, 1 RPS/conn, prompt ~20 tokens, run for 90s, collect perf samples with sampling_profiler=1.
tony: try toggling WRITEV_COALESCE=0/1 to see effect. if write coalescing reduced smallwrite syscall count, framing latency should drop.
lucy: ran toggle: with WRITEV_COALESCE=1 tail host drops ~6ms p95. with reverting shard count to 8 drops another ~7ms. combined gets us back to baseline.
sam: good repro. I'll start a bisect of PRs 1468..1500 focusing on 1476 and 1498.
andrew: can we also capture `strace -c -e writev` for a few requests and the http2 frame sizes? small frame sizes (<=128B) align with syscall overhead.
lucy: pushing traces to /tmp/host-flames/3419987654.tar.gz and uploading frame histogram to infra-artifacts.
perf-bot: [alert] canary 2024-10-15T09:12:00Z -> host preparse p50 +10ms, p95 +24ms for short-req cohort.
tonY: (typo) ignore
sam: action items: 1) revert batch_hint change in a canary to validate, 2) experiment with shard count knob (8/16) and add a gradual rollout, 3) add a micro e2e asserting host preparse p95 < 40ms for short requests, 4) instrument kvcache miss telemetry per shard.
andrew: i'll open rollback candidate for the preparse batch_hint and a config flag for shard_count with default 8. i'll also add a smallwrite metric to http2 framer.
lucy: thanks — will continue perf runs and attach updated flame. if bisect points to net coalesce as main contributor we'll treat that as separate fix.
sam: syncing tomorrow 09:00 PT for bisect findings. if we confirm regression, we'll pause the canary and roll back.
andrew: noted. adding ticket to infra board: HOST-PARSE-REGRESS-3419987654.
lucy: thanks team. short-term mitigation: revert batch_hint and roll shard_count back to 8 in canary. longer term: add prefix-aware sharding and async kvcache warmup.
